name: Question 20
worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4+4+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To normalize a vector x, we have to divide the vector by its norm: x‖x‖. Therefore, to normalize x, we first calculate ‖x‖ as follows:

‖x‖=x12+x22+x32+x42=(−1)2+22+22+42=1+4+4+16=25=5

Then, we divide x by its length:

x‖x‖=x5=15x=15[−1224]=[−15252545]
